open_points.subject: Browser access to Registry
open_points.text: “Browser — the Registry frontend from its own origin” contradicts “An instance reachable from beyond its host is a wrong deployment”
open_points.question: From where and through what network path does browser-executed frontend code reach Registry without making the instance reachable beyond its host?
options: The browser runs on the Registry host
A same-host frontend backend proxies browser requests to Registry
Registry is directly reachable from staff workstations on a private network
Registry is exposed through a host-level reverse proxy
open_points.default_guess: Use a same-host frontend backend as a credential-holding proxy to Registry.

open_points.subject: Membership of the trusted network
open_points.text: “the deployment's internal network” and “every unauthenticated read assumes the caller is inside”
open_points.question: Which machines, processes and services are considered inside this trusted network, and what prevents other deployment workloads from joining it and using the open reads?
options: Only host-local processes and explicitly attached same-host containers
Every machine on a private multi-host network
open_points.default_guess: Trust only host-local processes and explicitly attached containers on a dedicated same-host network.

open_points.subject: Frontend use of the staff credential
open_points.text: “How the frontend obtains the staff credential belongs to the frontend.”
open_points.question: Does browser code possess and present the configured staff credential, or does a trusted server-side frontend component authenticate staff and hold the credential on the browser's behalf?
options: Browser code holds the configured staff credential
Staff enter the credential for each browser session
A server-side frontend component holds it and gives the browser a separate session credential
open_points.default_guess: Use a server-side frontend component that holds the staff credential and authenticates browser sessions separately.

open_points.subject: Scope of project identity ownership
open_points.text: “Registry is the single living owner of a project's identity” conflicts with “Two instances share nothing” and “One physical object can therefore carry one id across instances”
open_points.question: When the same project id exists in independent instances, is either instance authoritative, are both independent authorities, or is an unnamed external actor responsible for keeping their identity data consistent?
options: Ownership is only single within each instance
One instance is authoritative and the others receive copies
An external caller is authoritative for cross-instance consistency
open_points.default_guess: Treat ownership as instance-local; matching ids across instances do not imply synchronized identity data.
